seal.statement: A preserved branch has never been proven and nothing tells its author. Since the non-main preservation fast path landed (79e8c7cb9 + 4c98b0a59, 2026-10-02/03) a git push of only non-main branch refs skips the local gate, and ci.yml runs only on pushes to main and on pull requests into main, so the branch's change cone runs nowhere: origin/quest/0-3-queryable-core-foundation carried a red hook test and a stage manifest that did not match the hook, its four stacked PRs (#88, #91, #95, #96, three of them with review/ heads) and the conflicting PR #74 got no CI, and a red direct commit sat on a landing branch until the publish gate caught it. The owner's decision (2026-10-04) is to run the CI change gate on quest/** and land/** pushes on self-hosted lab runners; measured on 2026-10-04 that path is not usable (the only runner registered to psvensson/lagrange is the offline GCP proof VM, no lab host is registered to any repository, the documented private control repository does not exist, and the repository is public), so this quest implements the owner's stated fallback and does not route the gate to GitHub-hosted runners: the fast path prints exactly one line saying the push is unproven, that the change gate (ci.yml) runs only on main and pull requests into main, and the command that proves the first pushed commit's cone (node scripts/lab.js test changed --lane all --split --sha <sha>, or a push with LAGRANGE_PUSH_PROVE_BRANCH=1). The line is not printed for a main push, for LAGRANGE_PUSH_PROVE_BRANCH=1, or for a deletion-only push, and its CI claim is bound to ci.yml's own triggers by a witness so it cannot outlive a change to them.

Design and security reasoning. A pull_request run uses the PR's own copy of ci.yml, so a fork PR can rewrite runs-on to [self-hosted]; on this public repository with approval_policy first_time_contributors, any contributor with one merged PR can reach every runner registered to the repository without an approval click. Trigger design (push-only routing, never pull_request) therefore cannot keep fork code off a lab host registered here - the protection must be where the runner is registered, which is why home-lab.md already forbids attaching home machines to this repository. The same exposure applies today to the GCP VM while it is awake (recorded for the owner; changing the approval policy or runner registration is an R26 action not taken). Requirements before the CI path can be enabled: (a) lab runners registered to the private control repository (or this repository's approval policy raised to all outside collaborators AND a lab-only label, an owner decision), with a dispatch from quest/** and land/** pushes and a status written back to the head sha (a new cross-repository token/secret); (b) the job must enter the lab's machine-wide lock: npm run check does not take it (only scripts/lab/probe.js and harness.js do), while thermal is gated per batch by run-classified-test-files; so the job should run node scripts/lab.js test changed on its own host rather than npm run check, or the lock recipe; (c) the proof base must be the merge-base with main: ci.yml's push range is github.event.before..HEAD and a new branch (before = zero sha) falls back to HEAD^, i.e. it would prove only the tip; (d) concurrency must cancel superseded non-main pushes (today cancel-in-progress is pull_request only, to keep main's exact-sha proofs); (e) stacked PR heads are mostly review/** (#88, #95, #96; #91 is quest/**), so a quest/** + land/** push trigger alone would not cover them. Alternative not taken: route quest/** and land/** to the GCP VM with a wake job - not lab, costs per push, needs id-token: write in ci.yml and a WIF attribute condition admitting non-main refs (unread), owner decision.

VERDICT: REJECT - one blocking usability defect (V4): the printed cone command fails in the preservation pattern the hint exists for. Everything else holds or is a non-blocking note.

V1 HOLDS. gh api (read-only): runners total_count 1 = lagrange-gcp-runner, labels self-hosted/Linux/X64/gcp, offline, persistent registration (same name while offline, so not ephemeral). Repo public, owner type User. fork-pr-contributor-approval = {"approval_policy":"first_time_contributors"} (endpoint readable). psvensson/lagrange-lab -> 404. Only repo variable DOCKERHUB_USERNAME. ci.yml:74 runs-on = push && head_commit contains '[ci:self-hosted]' ? 'self-hosted' : 'ubuntu-24.04'. Route is effectively dead: label self-hosted matches only the GCP VM, ci.yml has no wake job, so a marked push queues (GitHub keeps it up to 24 h) until full-gate.yml or the nightly formation-health.yml (cron 03:17, ran 10-02/03/04) wakes the VM - it would then run on whatever VM state exists, not on demand. Nuance: home-lab.md:248-250 says "Prefer a private control repository" and "Do not attach trusted home machines to pull-request workflows in the public Lagrange repository" - the author's "must never be attached to this repo" is a slight overstatement of the doc, but V2 shows the stronger reading is the correct one.

V2 HOLDS (reasoning correct) - and it yields a SECURITY FINDING (below). pull_request workflows (fork PRs included) run the workflow definition from the PR merge ref, so the PR's own ci.yml - including runs-on - is what executes; a user-owned repo has no runner groups to restrict a runner to selected workflows; so any runner registered to this repo is reachable by any fork PR that GitHub runs, and push-only routing expressions in ci.yml protect nothing (the fork edits the expression). ci.yml's own header comment (lines 17-20, "Pull requests always run GitHub-hosted regardless of any marker, because fork code ... must never reach a self-hosted runner") asserts a protection the expression cannot provide. Environments with required reviewers do not help either (the fork deletes the environment key). workflow_run / repository_dispatch relays are safe only if the runner is registered elsewhere (private control repo) - which is exactly the author's precondition (a), not a missed design. Missed/under-stated alternative: a cone on GitHub-hosted runners. The recorded owner rule (solve/epics/apparatus-release-consolidation.md:556-559, 2026-09-18) is "the corpus is never run on a GitHub-hosted runner while a local alternative exists, releases included"; scripts/select-change-tests.js:624 says the cone path "never runs the whole corpus", and ci.yml already runs the cone hosted for every PR and main push. So a hosted cone for quest/** + land/** does NOT violate the recorded rule; the quest's constraint never-hosted-for-the-cone is the author's stricter reading of the 2026-10-04 decision (which named self-hosted lab). It needs preconditions (c) merge-base range and (d) non-main cancellation too. This should be offered to the owner as an option, not foreclosed (non-blocking: the log's decision finding should say the recorded rule permits it).

V4 VIOLATED (blocking). scripts/lab/lagrange-lab.js commandTest -> probe.js labTestCommit plans the named sha in a throwaway worktree (fine for any sha), but runLabTest (probe.js:2607) throws "lab test: the controller runs its lanes in this tree, which is not exactly <sha>" whenever any share is placed on the controller and commitAt(root) != sha; commitAt (probe.js:2246) is null for ANY `git status --porcelain` output, untracked files included. With --split, placeLabLanes (probe.js:2478-2495) gives the exclusive lane to the fastest lab host and the rest to min(controller, others) by speed; today's fleet: controller x1.00, best lab host tv-dator x1.43 - so the controller always takes a share. Stub-driven runLabTest confirmed: commitAt null or another sha -> that error; equal -> proceeds. Outcomes: checkout clean at the pushed sha -> works (if the generated import graph exists there; a normal checkout usually has it, a fresh worktree does not - author's 1 red, reproduced: push-gate-change-proof 14/18 with "import graph is not generated" before refresh, 18/18 after); clean at the sha but untracked files -> fails; dirty or at another commit -> fails. It fails loudly, never runs something else. But the preservation pattern this hint targets - pushing a WIP sha that is not the checked-out HEAD, or from a tree with staged/untracked work - is exactly the failing case: the author's own live demonstration pushed 04e16ef99 from a worktree at d60c30921 with a staged delta, where the printed command would refuse; the author had to make a separate detached worktree (and then hit the import-graph trap). Minimal failing scenario: in .worktrees/q-branch-ci, run the printed `node scripts/lab.js test changed --lane all --split --sha 04e16ef99` -> refused after fleet discovery. Smallest corrective change: state the precondition in the line, e.g. "... --sha <sha> from a clean checkout at <sha> (or push with LAGRANGE_PUSH_PROVE_BRANCH=1)", pin it in one-hint-names-the-cone, and have the runbook paragraph name both prerequisites (clean tree exactly at the sha, untracked files included; generated import graph via npm run -s test:metadata:refresh in a fresh worktree). (Making lab test run the controller share in the planning checkout when --sha is named would remove the precondition, but that is a test-placement owner change - separate quest.)

SECURITY FINDING (owner): any fork PR from a non-first-time contributor runs without an approval click and executes its own ci.yml, so it can set runs-on: [self-hosted, gcp] and land a job on the GCP proof VM (persistent registration). The VM is offline most of the day, but the job stays queued up to 24 h and the nightly formation-health wake (03:17) hands it the VM - the same machine that holds GCP credentials for formation runs and, in formation-health's health job, a contents:write GITHUB_TOKEN persisted in the checkout. Today it is latent: the only contributors are psvensson, the `claude` account (one authored commit, noreply@anthropic.com) and github-actions[bot]; every other account is still first-time and needs a click - the click approves the PR's rewritten workflow. Merging any outsider's PR once makes that account click-free. Closes it: approval_policy all_external_contributors (`gh api -X PUT repos/psvensson/lagrange/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval -f approval_policy=all_external_contributors`), and structurally: no self-hosted runner registered to this public repo (move the GCP runner behind a private control repo, or register it just-in-time per wake and deregister after). Also correct ci.yml:17-20's false claim. Not tested; R26 - owner action.

Owner decisions: (1) raise fork approval to all_external_contributors - recommend yes, now. (2) where the GCP runner is registered - recommend the private control repo (psvensson/lagrange-lab) for GCP and lab hosts. (3) branch cone path - recommend a hosted ci.yml cone for quest/** + land/** now (allowed by the recorded rule, safe, needs merge-base range and non-main cancellation), lab via the control repo later. (4) prefix coverage - review/** and core/** carry more src/ work than quest/** + land/**; recommend including review/**. (5) retire or wake-enable the [ci:self-hosted] route - recommend retiring it (dead and the route's PR comment is false).

Owner decisions 2026-10-04 after the verifier's report (relayed by the lead): D1 preserved branches get their change CONE on GitHub-hosted runners now (cone only, never the corpus); lab runners via a private control repository are later, separate work. D2 prefixes covered: quest/**, land/** and review/**; wip/** and everything else stay free of CI. D3 retire the dead [ci:self-hosted] commit-message route entirely (ci.yml runs-on expression, publish-head --runner self-hosted and its marker validation, action-authority ROUTE_SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER, the ci-resource-plan literal, docs, the test pins, and ci.yml's false header comment that pull requests can never reach a self-hosted runner); ci.yml must then have no path by which any event selects a self-hosted runner. D4 keep the pre-push hint, corrected for V4 (clean checkout at <sha>, import-graph prerequisite in the runbook) and true for the new triggers. The owner separately raised fork-pr approval to all_external_contributors. This changes the sealed target (the statement says the CI path is not delivered and its constraint never-hosted-for-the-cone forbids D1), so the quest is superseded rather than reread (R09).

The owner's 2026-10-04 decisions D1-D4 replace this quest's sealed target: its statement delivers only the fallback hint and its constraints never-hosted-for-the-cone and 'ci.yml triggers unchanged' forbid the hosted branch cone the owner now requires. The successor seals D1-D4 as one statement; the measurements and findings above (self-hosted census, security reasoning, preconditions (a)-(e), branch-prefix census, ref/runner census) carry forward by reference and are not restated.
